sections.title: The Intuitive Hook: The Smoothie Analogy (0:00-0:45)
sections.content: Introduce the concept of decomposition. Just as a smoothie can be deconstructed into its original ingredients, any complex signal can be broken down into simple sine waves.
sections.example: Visualizing a 'Berry-Banana-Kale' smoothie being separated back into three distinct piles of fruit.

sections.title: Prerequisite Recap: Rotating Vectors (0:45-1:30)
sections.content: Briefly revisit Euler’s Formula (e^ix = cos x + i sin x). Explain how a signal can be visualized as a point rotating around a circle at different frequencies.
sections.example: An animation of a vector spinning; the 'shadow' cast on the X-axis creates a sine wave.

sections.title: The Mechanism: The Center of Mass (1:30-3:00)
sections.content: Explain the Fourier Transform as a tool that 'wraps' a signal around a center point at a specific frequency. If the frequency matches the signal's component, the center of mass shifts away from the origin.
sections.example: A complex wave of a chirping bird 'wrapped' around a circle. When the rotation speed matches the bird's pitch, the center of mass spikes—revealing the frequency.

sections.title: Key Concept: Time Domain vs. Frequency Domain (3:00-4:00)
sections.content: Contrast the Time Domain (where things happen) with the Frequency Domain (what things are made of). Emphasize that the Fourier Transform is the bridge between these two views.
sections.example: Side-by-side animation: A piano keyboard playing a chord (Time Domain) vs. a bar chart showing the specific notes being played (Frequency Domain).

sections.title: Application: Real-World Filtering (4:00-5:00)
sections.content: Demonstrate why this matters. If we can see the frequencies, we can remove the ones we don't want (Noise Cancellation).
sections.example: A smartphone character filtering out 'background construction noise' from a voice recording by simply erasing the high-frequency spikes in the Frequency Domain.

storyboard.title: The Intuitive Hook: The Smoothie Analogy (0:00-0:45)
lecture_lines: A smoothie is just combined ingredients.
Signals are just combined sine waves.
Decompose them to find the ingredients.
animations: Fade in a blender icon #FFFFFF at center.
Display ingredients (vector arrows) in #FF5733 #33FF57 #3357FF around the blender.
Animate ingredients merging into the blender center.

storyboard.title: Prerequisite Recap: Rotating Vectors (0:45-1:30)
lecture_lines: Euler's formula connects circles and sine.
A vector rotating creates a wave.
animations: Display two basis vectors i-hat #FFFF00 and j-hat #00FFFF.
Rotate i-hat and j-hat by 90 degrees counter-clockwise.
Highlight the path traced by the rotation using light gray #AAAAAA arcs.

storyboard.title: The Mechanism: The Center of Mass (1:30-3:00)
lecture_lines: Wrap a signal around a circle.
Adjust frequency to match the signal.
The Fourier transform acts as prism.
animations: Place a set of points (masses) #FFFFFF in a 2D plane.
Calculate and draw the centroid (center of mass) in #FF00FF.
Move the points and show the centroid reacting in real-time.

storyboard.title: Key Concept: Time Domain vs. Frequency Domain (3:00-4:00)
lecture_lines: Time domain shows how things happen.
Frequency domain shows what things are.
Fourier transform bridges these two views.
animations: Display time-domain and frequency-domain plots side-by-side.

storyboard.title: Application: Real-World Filtering (4:00-5:00)
lecture_lines: Unwanted noise has unique high frequencies.
Remove these to clear your audio.
animations: Render a noisy signal #FF0000 on a graph.
Apply a low-pass filter (represented by a shaded block) #FFFFFF.
